canonical-property.definition: A standard-track CSS property recognized by the PandamStyle descriptor catalog. Recognition never grants consumer access to arbitrary values.
canonical-property.proof: Required entries: accepted finite domains and structured rejections (E2), emitted and transformed CSS (E3) and computed behavior in each profile target (E4). Recognized but not required entries: either the same proof when admitted, or a structured diagnostic fixture (E2).

normalized-alias.definition: An unprefixed spelling of exactly one canonical property or scoped platform extension with a curated positive equivalence statement and sources: a specified legacy name alias, an engine-declared alias or an upstream authoring key whose compiler source rewrites it to the target. Vendor-prefixed names are never normalized aliases. The canonical property carries the requirement.
normalized-alias.proof: Normalization or a diagnostic naming the canonical property (E2), and emitted CSS equivalent to the canonical form (E3). CE-02 decides whether the spelling is accepted or diagnosed; prefix emission belongs to the CE-01 transformation.

system-resource.definition: Expressed through a design-system-owned resource (typed custom property, font-face descriptor, gradient, mask, shadow, filter or transform composition, focus treatment or declaration bundle) rather than a free property value.
system-resource.proof: Resource definition admission and reference resolution (E2) and emitted CSS (E3); computed behavior (E4) through the carrying capability's proof record.

scoped-platform-extension.definition: A vendor or platform property without a portable standard equivalent that a named profile scopes explicitly, such as Electron drag regions.
scoped-platform-extension.proof: Scoped admission (E2), emitted CSS (E3) and computed behavior on the exact platform engine (E4) when required; otherwise a scoped diagnostic (E2).

deprecated-or-experimental.definition: Deprecated, experimental, non-standard, abandoned-draft, unimplemented-specification, obsolete-engine-prefix, vendor-legacy-variant, divergent-legacy-variant or superseded-name entries. A vendor legacy variant is a -webkit-/-moz- name related by BCD to a canonical target; agents author the target, and any prefixed emission is a CE-01 transformation. A divergent legacy variant additionally has a documented grammar or value difference. A superseded name is an unprefixed historical name without established equivalence. They remain in the denominator with a replacement where one exists.
deprecated-or-experimental.proof: A structured diagnostic fixture naming the replacement (E2). Experimental entries also need a CE-11 target fact record (E1) before any promotion. A vendor or divergent legacy variant whose prefixed form still ships in some engine (emissionDecision D-BP-07) also needs emitted-CSS proof (E3) restricted to the value subset it shares with its target.

non-css-syntax.definition: An upstream authoring key that is not a CSS property: selector, condition, pseudo-element, axis or multi-property helpers, development helpers and theme keys.
non-css-syntax.proof: An equivalent-capability fixture through canonical PandamStyle mechanisms, or a diagnostic (E2), plus emitted CSS for the equivalent (E3).

incompatible-runtime-requirement.definition: Behavior that requires runtime script binding or unbounded runtime values. It has no static CSS equivalent.
incompatible-runtime-requirement.proof: A negative diagnostic fixture (E2) and a visible limitation record.

procedure: 1. Curated records win in this order: incompatibleRuntime, systemResources, nonCssSyntax, platformExtensions, aliases (unprefixed only, each with a positive equivalence statement and sources), deprecated, experimental, nonstandard.
2. Names with an obsolete-engine prefix (-ms-, -o-, -khtml-) are deprecated-or-experimental/obsolete-engine-prefix; their current equivalent is recorded, CE-01 owns the engine incompatibility.
3. Otherwise a BCD css.properties status decides: standard track and neither deprecated nor experimental is a canonical property; deprecated, experimental and non-standard keep that subkind.

4. A name without BCD status that BCD records as a prefix or alternative name of another property relates to that target. If the target is not canonical, the name inherits the target's deprecated or experimental disposition. Otherwise the absence of a BCD note is never treated as equivalence: (a) a vendor-prefixed name is never a normalized alias; it is deprecated-or-experimental/vendor-legacy-variant, or divergent-legacy-variant when an aliasAudit grammar-divergent verdict cites a BCD note, engine source or specification; (b) an unprefixed name needs an aliasAudit verdict: equivalent with a positive equivalence statement and sources keeps it a normalized alias, grammar-divergent makes it a divergent-legacy-variant, superseded makes it deprecated-or-experimental/superseded-name. Relating statements with notes, partial implementation or flags always need a verdict, and an equivalent or behavior-caveat-only verdict on notes that mention syntax or values needs grammarHintReviewed. Missing, stale or source-less verdicts fail the build. Prefixed emission for targets is the CE-01 transformation (D-BP-07), not an authoring alias.
5. A remaining -webkit-/-moz- name whose unprefixed base is an inventory entry follows its base in the same way; a vendor-only name is deprecated-or-experimental/nonstandard.

6. Any remaining name is a build error. Every entry must also match exactly one family; the family supplies the capability family, the owner of canonical/platform entries and the profiles that require them.

7. An entry's capability family is its curated requirementCarrier, else its family's. Its owner is curated, else set by disposition subkind (aliases CE-02), else its family's owner; the owner must belong to that capability's coverage Work lots, except CAP-01 and the CE-01/CE-02/CE-11 disposition owners of non-canonical entries.
8. overlayRequirements add the rtl and svg-media overlay profiles to a canonical entry that some application profile already requires and that matches the overlay's names or patterns.

behavior.reason: Internet Explorer HTML Components attach script behavior through CSS. PandamStyle emits static CSS and has no script-binding channel.

-moz-binding.reason: Removed XBL binding attaches script/DOM behavior through CSS. No static CSS equivalent exists.

custom-property.note: BCD placeholder for --*. Only system-owned typed variables are admissible; an arbitrary consumer custom property or runtime value is LIM-01.

notes.-webkit-box-orient: Deprecated as authoring input, but part of the emitted -webkit-line-clamp bundle Panda produces for line-clamp; CE-06 decides the bundle.
notes.-webkit-line-clamp: BCD records only prefixed release support for line-clamp in Chrome, Firefox and Safari; the canonical line-clamp needs the CE-06 bundle decision.
notes.-webkit-mask-composite: Non-standard grammar differing from mask-composite; Panda emits it beside mask-composite. Emission-only under CE-01 transformation policy.
notes.x: SVG geometry property in BCD. Panda 2.2.0 maps its x utility to --translate-x instead; that upstream key conflict is not an alias.
notes.y: SVG geometry property in BCD. Panda 2.2.0 maps its y utility to --translate-y instead; that upstream key conflict is not an alias.
notes.speak: Standard-track in BCD but outside every accepted profile.
notes.all: Requires complete reset/conflict semantics before admission; StyleX 0.19.1 rejects it and Panda passes it through.

rtl.description: A canonical entry already required by an application profile is also required in the rtl overlay when it is direction- or writing-mode-sensitive: logical properties, start/end values and properties whose computed result depends on direction.

svg-media.description: A canonical entry already required by an application profile is also required in the svg-media overlay when it styles replaced content, images or SVG.

-moz-background-clip.reason: BCD: Firefox used the padding | border value syntax, not the standard box keywords.

-moz-background-origin.reason: BCD: Firefox used the padding | border value syntax, not the standard box keywords.

-moz-border-image.reason: BCD: before Firefox 15 an earlier version of the specification was implemented.

-moz-box-sizing.reason: BCD note is a getComputedStyle bug before Firefox 23; the value grammar is that of box-sizing.

-moz-column-count.reason: BCD note is a display: table-caption bug before version 37; same grammar.

-moz-column-rule.reason: BCD: before Firefox 3 the normal keyword had a different default value (0, not 1em).

-moz-column-width.reason: BCD note is a display: table-caption bug before version 37; same grammar.

-moz-columns.reason: BCD note is a display: table-caption bug before version 37; same grammar.

-moz-font-feature-settings.reason: BCD: Firefox 4 to 14 supported an older, different syntax.

-webkit-animation.reason: BCD note concerns animation-fill-mode support in Android below 2.3; same grammar.

-webkit-background-clip.reason: BCD: the prefixed property accepts the extra value synonyms padding, border and content.

-webkit-background-origin.reason: BCD: the prefixed property accepts the extra value synonyms padding, border and content.

-webkit-background-size.reason: BCD: an older draft where an omitted second value duplicates the first and contain/cover are absent.

-webkit-border-image.reason: Always includes the fill keyword in border-image-slice, and length values in border-image-width override the corresponding border-*-width.

sources.statement: Differs from border-image in that it always includes the 'fill' keyword and makes border-image-width lengths override border-*-width.

-webkit-border-radius.reason: Two lengths are read as horizontal and vertical radii: '-webkit-border-radius: l1 l2' equals 'border-radius: l1 / l2'.

sources.statement: Differs from border-radius only in the interpretation of a value consisting of two lengths.

-webkit-box-decoration-break.reason: BCD partial implementation applies only to inline elements; same grammar. The restriction is a target fact of box-decoration-break (D-BP-07).

-webkit-font-feature-settings.reason: BCD note records that Firefox 129 added the alias for compatibility; same grammar.

-webkit-initial-letter.reason: BCD: the prefixed WebKit form does not accept decimal values.

-webkit-line-clamp.reason: Legacy shorthand with syntax none | <integer [1,inf]> that sets continue to -webkit-discard and block-ellipsis to auto, unlike line-clamp.

sources.statement: -webkit-line-clamp has the syntax none | <integer [1,inf]>, sets continue to -webkit-discard and unconditionally sets block-ellipsis to auto, unlike line-clamp.
Non-standard shorthand of max-lines, block-ellipsis and continue with grammar none | <integer [1,inf]>.

-webkit-mask.reason: BCD: a different shorthand syntax that also sets the non-standard -webkit-mask-attachment.

-webkit-mask-image.reason: BCD: engines initially accepted only -webkit- prefixed gradient values.

-webkit-perspective.reason: BCD: Firefox accepts unitless values for the prefixed form only.

-webkit-print-color-adjust.reason: BCD notes are printing behavior of the body background and clipped sprites; same grammar.

-webkit-ruby-position.reason: BCD: legacy before/after values whose meaning depends on ruby-align, not the standard over/under/inter-character values.

-webkit-scroll-snap-type.reason: BCD: older Safari implements an earlier draft without axis values.

-webkit-transform.reason: BCD note is an Android 2.3 form-input bug; same grammar.
